title: Tokyo's Sushi Bus Combines Food and Sightseeing
paragraphs: Visitors to Tokyo will soon be able to enjoy two Japanese experiences at once — sightseeing around the city and eating conveyor belt sushi.

Sushi Bus is a new sightseeing bus that will begin running in Tokyo in October. The company behind the project, Sushi Bus Co., says it's the world's first double-decker bus with a conveyor belt sushi system.
The bus will have 20 seats on its open-top second floor. During the 70-minute trip, passengers will travel around Tokyo and be able to eat as much sushi as they want.

The sushi will be made in a kitchen on the first floor of the bus. It will then be sent to the second floor using an elevator. A member of staff will put the sushi onto a conveyor belt that goes by the seats, and passengers can then choose sushi from the conveyor belt as the bus moves through the city.

The bus will start and finish near Tokyo Station. It will travel around the city while passengers eat sushi and see famous Tokyo landmarks, such as Shibuya Scramble Crossing and the Kaminarimon Gate in Asakusa.
The company says Sushi Bus is aimed at international tourists. The bus can also prepare food for people with allergies or those who can't eat certain foods for religious reasons.
For now, the company plans to start with just one bus. In the future, it hopes to add more buses and bring Sushi Bus to other tourist areas in Japan, including Osaka and Kyoto.
